vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_002: Does vitamin D deficiency affect implant healing?
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_003: Yes, low 25-OH vitamin D levels can negatively affect bone healing after implant placement. Studies show that patients with serum values ​​below 20 ng/ml are significantly more likely to suffer early losses than patients with sufficient values ​​above 30 ng/ml.
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_004: Why supplement D3 together with K2?
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_005: Vitamin K2 (MK-7) directs the increased calcium absorbed by D3 into the bones by activating osteocalcin. Without K2 there is theoretically a risk of vascular calcification. The combination is particularly useful with longer supplementation and higher D3 doses.
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_006: How common is vitamin D deficiency in Germany?
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_007: The Robert Koch Institute classifies around 30% of the adult population as having inadequate blood supply (below 30 nmol/l or 12 ng/ml). The situation worsens significantly in the winter months - around 60% do not achieve adequate levels.
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_008: What vitamin D level is recommended before implantation?
vitamin_d3_implantology.copy_009: For optimal osseointegration, current studies recommend a 25-OH-D serum level of at least 30 ng/ml (75 nmol/l), ideally 40-60 ng/ml. A higher target value may make sense for high-risk patients with diabetes or osteoporosis.
